messages:
kevin: Heads-up: I want to run a strict one-to-one model comparison today to isolate kernel selection + batching heuristics + KV cache behavior. Need sign-off on methodology.

maria: Scope? replay traces only or synthetic as well? tokenizer alignment concerns?

kevin: Both. Plan: 1) Replay harness using exact user traces 2) Synthetic generator seeded to match seq-length distribution from the traces. Must use identical prompts, decoding params, and stop sequences. Ensure tokenizer encoding is identical across runtimes (use tokenizer.encode(..., add_special_tokens=False)).

sam: For decoding let's avoid sampling noise — use greedy (temp=0) and top_p=0 for deterministic runs. If we need stochastic tests, do a separate pass with fixed seeds.

diane: We'll need explicit kernel overrides vs auto selection. Run three kernel modes: forced-opt, forced-fallback, and auto. Example run (replay):
```
./harness/replay --trace traces/2025-12-01.json \
  --model rwin-7b-q4f --decode greedy --temp 0 --top_p 0 \
  --kernel-mode forced-opt --batching-policy latency_target=20ms \
  --out /tmp/bench/1860004321/forced-opt.log
```

alex: Also measure cold vs warm: 1) cold (fresh process, empty KV) 2) warmed (run N warm requests). We should capture both. I suggest --kv-warmup-requests=1000 or run 10 unique prefixes until steady token/sec observed.

perf-bot: perf-bot: kickstarted bench 1860004321 (replay + synthetic). Will post summaries and artifacts here when done. :runner:

maria: For synthetic traffic, sample sequence lengths from the replay histogram (preserve short/med/long ratios). Run three batching strategies: constant-batch (fixed N), latency-targeted (max latency SLO 20ms), and cost-targeted (maximize throughput under p95 latency cap).

sam: Instrumentation: capture per-token breakdown (kernel_ms, memcpy_ms, scheduler_ms, kv_lookup_ms). Use nvtx + our light tracer; add a periodic nvprof snapshot on a subset of runs. Example capture flags: --tracer=light --nvtx=true --nvprof-sample=50

diane: Baseline commit to compare against: 7a1f2c (last green). Metrics to record: p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, kernel time ratio, memcpy ratio. If p95 regresses >5% vs baseline, auto-open perf ticket and attach repro.

kevin: Good. I'll kick off at 12:30 UTC. We need a 200-prompt eval set that covers short/medium/long conversational prompts. Any suggestions?

alex: I already curated one: /shared/bench/promptsets/one_to_one_200.json (contains tags short/med/long and expected stop-seqs).

maria: Reminder from last time: tokenizer mismatch between HF-fast and LlamaTokenizer caused a 2-3% perf delta (different tokenization -> different kv hit patterns). Double-check vocab/merge rules and ensure both runtimes use the exact same tokenization codepath.

perf-bot: perf-bot: first-pass finished: greedy tokens/sec (warm, forced-opt): 1023 t/s, p95 latency (forced-opt vs auto): +8% on auto, memcpy skew +12%. Artifacts: http://perf.local/reports/1860004321/logs.tar.gz

sam: +8% p95 on auto is concerning. Is memcpy the primary offender? Can we see the kernel breakdown?

diane: I'll open perf/regressions/1860004321 and attach the logs. Tagging runtime-kernel and kv teams. Reproducer + nvprof snapshot included.

kevin: Thanks. If anyone sees anything to change in the harness or metric definitions before I start the larger sweep, call it out now.

maria: Two small asks: 1) add a strict tokenizer hash to artifacts (commit + tokenizer version) 2) include seed + decode params in the top-level meta.json that we upload.

kevin: Done — harness will write meta.json with commit, tokenizer_hash, decode_params, kernel_mode, batching_policy.

perf-bot: perf-bot: full run complete. Summary file: http://perf.local/reports/1860004321/summary.html. Preliminary note: forced-opt wins throughput but auto falls back on memcpy-path for long sequences; KV warmup reduces p95 by ~6% across kernels.

sam: Ok let's triage kernel selection falling back to memcpy for long sequences. @diane can you assign to kernel team?

diane: On it. Creating kernel ticket and linking this thread.

kevin: Appreciate everyone. We'll use this as the standard methodology for future one-to-one comparisons. Short follow-ups in thread as folks debug.
